feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: Breaking news, top national and world stories, politics, business and culture from NPR. Catch up on demand with NPR News Now, Up First and Consider This.

entry.title: Discursive Verses: Is 'Spend Dat' the best financial indicator of America's grift economy?
entry.summary: NPR Music culture critic and reporter Rodney Carmichael ruminates on the latest in rap culture. This week: How Yung Miami's summer bop became a sweeping indictment.

entry.title: Russell Brand is convicted of rape, and judge says he'll get a prison term
entry.summary: A prosecutor described Brand as a ruthless, calculating, manipulative "sexual predator." Brand, 51, denied the charges, saying he had never forced anyone to do something against their will.

entry.title: First-time homebuyers remain scarce, but a record share of them pay all cash
entry.summary: A new report finds generational wealth is widening the divide between homebuyers and those priced out. The median age of first-time buyers also remains at a record high.

entry.title: Teens worldwide aren't getting enough exercise -- especially girls
entry.summary: A new study looks at the recommended amount of daily exercise for adolescents — and how few are getting it.

entry.title: What's next for Democrats after the midterms. And, a look at the outstanding races
entry.summary: Democrats have regained control of Congress. They have a long list of investigations into Trump planned. And, not all races have been called. Here's a look at how they could affect the Dems' majority.

entry.title: Sen. Gillibrand says Democrats must end Iran war, hold Trump accountable. But how?
entry.summary: Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand spoke with Morning Edition about Democrats' priorities, from lowering costs to ending the Iran war. But questions remain about how they'll deliver.

entry.title: Trump's arch is on the verge of federal approval. But a judge could block construction
entry.summary: A federal panel will meet to consider the arch for final approval on Thursday, and the government said it may begin construction later that same day. Critics hope a judge will intervene last-minute.

entry.title: As budgets tighten, people are breaking out their library cards
entry.summary: Some Americans squeezed by high prices are relying more on their local libraries for things like books, streaming services and high-priced items like musical instruments and sewing machines.

entry.title: The South flexes political power in midterms, sets regional influence in 2028 election
entry.summary: Tuesday's dramatic midterm results have transformed the electoral map, ensuring the path to future power for Democrats and Republicans must run through the South and its diverse voting population.

entry.title: Does the blue wave mean lower gasoline and diesel prices soon? Don't hold your breath
entry.summary: A new Democratic majority in Congress could pressure the president to end the war in Iran. But it will be harder for them to directly affect fuel prices, which are tied to a complex international oil market.
